questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise can:

options.text: Is recommended.
Cause hearing loss.
Is not harmful.
Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Ignore them.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up makes them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you must:

options.text: You may exceed the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may disregard "No passing zone" markings if the pass was started in a passing zone.
You may pass on the shoulder.
Complete the pass within the posted speed limits and only in a legal passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass within the posted speed limits and only in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: Always complete a pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Do not ride directly alongside another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be difficult to see what is happening behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: When you ride alongside a vehicle, you may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver cannot see you and may hit you. You also lose your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When using a motorcycle that is new to you, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good riding condition.
Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
Ride as you usually do, since most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before you ride, practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Learn where the gears are.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing or stopping to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: The only way to remove alcohol from your body is through:

options.text: Time.
Drinking coffee.
Exercising.
Taking a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Time.
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. There is no way to speed up the process.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to happen to:

options.text: Experienced riders.
Beginning riders.
Those familiar with their motorcycle.
Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to new riders who have no training and do not know their motorcycle.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to hazards ahead.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. They tell you the legal speed limit and you must obey them.

questions.question: Which of these clothing items will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury, riders should wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: A cushion of space around your motorcycle helps to:

options.text: Give you time to react to hazards.
Hide you from other drivers.
Prevent you from avoiding hazards.
Allow you to look at road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: It helps you see farther ahead.
It makes it harder to see ahead.
It makes it difficult to see beyond the vehicle.
It allows the other driver to speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see farther ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to see farther ahead and to make yourself more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see better and be seen by others.
Be close to the road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see better and be seen by others.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Which of these surfaces does NOT have poor traction?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all have poor traction. Dry pavement is safer for motorcycles.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle:

options.text: Is a useless action.
Can slow you down by using engine braking.
Is illegal.
Should not be done if other vehicles are around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can slow you down by using engine braking.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through smooth downshifting is useful. If you use engine braking, activate your brake lights separately to alert other drivers that you are slowing down.

questions.question: In general, the body eliminates almost ______ of alcohol per hour.

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink
questions.explanation: A person's body can remove the alcohol from about one drink per hour on average.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Be made of soft material.
Be made of heavy material.
Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some leg.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants that cover your entire legs and are made of leather or sturdy synthetic material. Clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it restricts movement.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let them.
Encourage them to use quiet roads.
Not get involved.
Take their keys.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take their keys.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride if they have had too much to drink. Do whatever you can to stop them, including taking their keys if necessary. Arrange another way for them to get home.

questions.question: When riding, goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Are not as effective as eyeglasses.
Do not provide any protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield protects your entire face. Eyeglasses do not provide adequate protection for either your eyes or face.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping a group of riders small?

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
A small group can break traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always be trying to catch up to the group.
It will be difficult to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups have several advantages. Other vehicles can pass a small group safely more easily. A small group is less likely to get separated by traffic or stop lights. Slower riders don't need to rush to keep up.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, you must be able to see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane behind you.
Only the lane next to you.
Most of your helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. A properly adjusted mirror may show the edge of your arm or shoulder. What matters most is seeing the road behind and to the side of you.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots. What should you do about them?

options.text: They don't have blind spots because they are small.
They have blind spots, but they are too small to matter.
Check them regularly before changing lanes.
They are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular part of how you watch the road.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not ask your passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn drivers a passenger is aboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle has a seat designed for two riders. The motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear you wear.

questions.question: Why should you maintain an adequate following distance behind other vehicles?

options.text: To give yourself time and space to see and react to hazards.
So you can tailgate.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give yourself time and space to see and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A good following distance gives you enough space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. Extra space also lets you see road hazards better, like potholes.
